item.title: Downtown Grand Rapids hotel hosts Valentine's Day-themed silent disco
item.description: On Feb. 13, visitors to the JW Marriott Grand Rapids hotel and its main ballroom can attend My Bloody Valentine, a silent disco from Ice Guru Events.

item.title: Otsego students teach Anne Frank's story to peers with exhibit
item.description: Students in Allegan County are learning history in a special way, acting as guides to help tell the story of Anne Frank and the events of World War II.

item.title: Kalamazoo eyes urban density to tackle housing crisis
item.description: Kalamazoo City Commission got its first look at a study Monday night that leans into the potential of reimagining business corridors in the city.

item.title: What's known about the search for 'Today' host Savannah Guthrie's mother
item.description: “We believe now, after we processed that crime scene, that we do in fact have a crime scene, and we‘re asking the community‘s help,” the sheriff said.

item.title: Michigan judge charged in embezzlement scheme targeting vulnerable adults
item.description: Four people, including a sitting judge, have been charged in an alleged yearslong embezzlement scheme.

item.title: Michigan license plate cameras face backlash: Big help, or Big Brother?
item.description: In more than 125 cities and counties across Michigan, nondescript cameras perched near busy roadways snap a picture every time a car drives by.

item.title: 'Not safe ice': Officials warn against walking on Lake Michigan
item.description: Public Safety departments up and down the Lake Michigan shoreline this week are warning to stay off the ice after a rescue team in South Haven had to carry a slip-and-fall victim 100 yards back to shore.

item.title: Greenville police: Shooting victim identified suspect before dying
item.description: A man told Greenville police his roommate shot him before dying at the hospital Sunday, authorities say.

item.title: Former Adult Protective Services worker accused of scamming elderly women
item.description: Derek Plumb, a former APS employee with the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services, is accused of embezzling more than $100,000 from a vulnerable adult and four counts of forging a document affecting real property. The charges stem from Plumb’s alleged monthslong scheme to defraud three elderly women and transfer the deeds of their homes to himself.

item.title: Portage family left in cold due to propane delivery delay
item.description: A Portage family said they went more than a week without heat in below-freezing temperatures after their propane provider failed to refill their tank when promised, leaving their home colder than the outdoors.
